Subject: Vector index sync & rerank QA gating — Lighthouse pilot

Thanks all — quick kickoff note and a narrow set of asks so we can lock the pilot schedule. Goal: sync Lighthouse's existing vector index into the pilot Vector DB, run a rerank evaluation suite on a 10k-sample, and do a staged backfill to production with minimal user-visible regressions.

High-level proposals (attached: index-plan-v1.pdf):
- Index sync: incremental snapshot -> bulksync waves (5M/day target for initial backfill).
- Vector DB: recommend starting on managed cluster with cold-store support (we discussed Pinecone vs Weaviate; we'll defer to ops but need write throughput and TTL controls).
- Rerank gating: define a small metric set (MRR, Recall@10, latency p95 for model+reranker) and a pass/fail threshold.

Asks:
1) Carla / Lighthouse: confirm the 10k sample dataset (IDs + queries + labels) is ready and whether there are any GDPR-sensitive fields we should exclude.
2) Jordan: can you outline the rerank smoke tests & thresholds we should run?
3) Ben: ops constraints on ingestion rate and preferred shipping format (ndjson / signed URL flow).

Proposed schedule: staging backfill window Nov 8–10, production cutover Nov 12 (all tentative). If these fit, I'll prepare the action tracker and loop Naomi to coordinate CS comms.

Thanks,
Mina

Mina / Carla — thanks. Short answer to the gating question: we should use both a relative and absolute approach to protect Lighthouse UX while allowing improvements. Proposed gating logic (summary):
- Baseline: current production retrieval+ranking metrics on the sample (we'll compute MRR and Recall@10).
- Gate1 (smoke): no Regression > 2% absolute in Recall@10 and latency p95 (end-to-end) must not exceed 180ms on staging traffic profile.
- Gate2 (acceptance): MRR on pilot >= baseline - 1% OR MRR >= baseline + 0.5% (so small improvements allowed; larger drops block).
- Also run a manual spot-check with 100 queries (edge cases) for hallucination/noise.

On tests & infra:
- I'll produce rerank-eval-sample.json with the eval harness input (labels, features). We will run the reranker in an isolated staging cluster and log token-level latencies.
- We should checkpoint model versions & embed metadata (tokenizer/hash) so rollbacks map deterministically.

Open ops question: can we stream indices to the DB with pre-sharded tarballs containing 100k vectors each? That reduces write contention.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding ops constraints and a pragmatic ingestion suggestion.

Constraints:
- Managed cluster can accept ~2M vectors/hour per write node (50-100 dims typical). For a 10M initial index, plan for parallel workers or 24–48hr window.
- We need object storage access for pre-sharded uploads (signed URLs preferred).

Suggestion (ingest-playbook.md attached):
1) Export Lighthouse data as ndjson batches, 100k vectors per file, gzip compressed.
2) Upload blobs to our S3-compatible staging bucket via signed URL.
3) Ingestion workers (k8s job) will pull, validate, write via bulk upsert API and mark shards complete.
4) During cutover, put a short (5–10m) read-only freeze for the served index and then switch the route to the new index. If rollback needed, route back to previous index (we keep immutable snapshots).

I'll prepare the ingest scripts and a small perf test to characterize write throughput on the target DB; ETA for scripts: Nov 4.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
